title.en: The dawn ride and the hidden horse

heading.en: A knock at four in the morning

hook.en: Aram is woken before sunrise by his cousin, sitting on a magnificent white horse. Aram knows the family cannot afford a horse, so where did it come from?

objectives.en: Narrate the events of the dawn ride
Explain Aram's moral struggle about stealing
Describe how the boys hide the horse

narration.en: Aram is woken before sunrise by his cousin, sitting on a magnificent white horse. Aram knows the family cannot afford a horse, so where did it come from?

body.en: Early one morning Mourad wakes Aram and shows him a beautiful white horse. Aram longs to ride and is torn between joy and his knowledge that the horse must have been stolen. The boys ride together through the countryside in the early light.

points.en: Mourad appears at dawn on a white horse
Aram's longing to ride since childhood
Joy and freedom of the ride

narration.en: Early one morning Mourad wakes Aram and shows him a beautiful white horse. Aram longs to ride and is torn between joy and his knowledge that the horse must have been stolen. The boys ride together through the countryside in the early light.
Let us place the morning's events on a timeline.

say.en: Mourad wakes Aram very early in the morning.
Outside stands a beautiful white horse.
Aram wonders whether this is stealing, and argues himself out of it.
The boys ride together through the countryside.
Aram rides alone, is thrown, and the horse runs off.
Mourad recovers it, and they hide it in an old vineyard barn.

text.en: Horse hidden in an old barn

body.en: Aram reasons that it is not really stealing because they do not mean to sell the horse; this childish logic lets him enjoy the adventure. When he rides alone, the horse throws him and runs off, and Mourad later brings it back. The boys hide the horse in the barn of an abandoned vineyard.

points.en: Aram's logic: not stealing unless the horse is sold
Aram's solo ride: thrown off; Mourad recovers the horse
Hiding place: barn of a deserted vineyard

narration.en: Aram reasons that it is not really stealing because they do not mean to sell the horse; this childish logic lets him enjoy the adventure. When he rides alone, the horse throws him and runs off, and Mourad later brings it back. The boys hide the horse in the barn of an abandoned vineyard.

problem.en: How does Aram convince himself that riding the horse is not stealing?

steps.en: Aram knows the family is too poor to buy a horse.
He also knows the family is proud of its honesty.
He decides it is not stealing as long as they do not sell the horse.

answer.en: Aram knows his poor family could never buy such a horse, yet they are famously honest. He resolves the conflict with childish logic: it would only be stealing if they offered the horse for sale, so riding it is not a crime.
